content.text: In this trace the travel-service GET waits about 2.3 s before route-service receives it; route-service itself answers in about 10 ms. I'll measure that send-to-receive gap across every client→server pair to see which connections carry it.

input.query: WITH c AS (SELECT trace_id, span_id, service_name cs, span_name cn, time ct, duration cd FROM abnormal_traces WHERE attr_span_kind='Client'), s AS (SELECT trace_id, parent_span_id, service_name ss, span_name sn, time st, duration sd FROM abnormal_traces WHERE attr_span_kind='Server') SELECT cs caller, ss callee, sn callee_span, count(*) n, approx_quantile(extract(epoch FROM (st-ct))*1000,0.5) gap_ms_p50, approx_quantile(extract(epoch FROM (st-ct))*1000,0.95) gap_ms_p95, approx_quantile(cd/1e6,0.5) client_p50, approx_quantile(sd/1e6,0.5) server_p50 FROM c JOIN s ON s.trace_id=c.trace_id AND s.parent_span_id=c.span_id GROUP BY ALL HAVING gap_ms_p95 > 50 ORDER BY n DESC

content.text: The travel→route GET is the only edge with a large pre-send gap. I'll check the network-level (hubble) metrics for travel→route and for the route-plan and basic-service connections to tell network from HTTP-layer delay.

input.query: SELECT 'ab' p, metric, attr_source, attr_destination, count(*) n, avg(value) avgv, max(value) maxv FROM abnormal_metrics_sum WHERE metric LIKE 'hubble%' AND (attr_source LIKE '%travel-service%' OR attr_destination LIKE '%travel-service%' OR attr_source LIKE '%route-service%' OR attr_destination LIKE '%route-service%') GROUP BY ALL UNION ALL SELECT 'no', metric, attr_source, attr_destination, count(*), avg(value), max(value) FROM normal_metrics_sum WHERE metric LIKE 'hubble%' AND (attr_source LIKE '%travel-service%' OR attr_destination LIKE '%travel-service%' OR attr_source LIKE '%route-service%' OR attr_destination LIKE '%route-service%') GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY 2,3,4,1

input.query: SELECT 'ab' p, metric, attr_source, attr_destination, round(avg(value),1) avgv, round(max(value),1) maxv, count(*) n FROM abnormal_metrics_sum WHERE metric LIKE 'hubble%' AND attr_source LIKE '%travel-service%' AND attr_destination LIKE '%route-service%' GROUP BY ALL UNION ALL SELECT 'no', metric, attr_source, attr_destination, round(avg(value),1), round(max(value),1), count(*) FROM normal_metrics_sum WHERE metric LIKE 'hubble%' AND attr_source LIKE '%travel-service%' AND attr_destination LIKE '%route-service%' GROUP BY ALL

content.text: This trace is mostly normal, so the basic-service slowness is not explained by it. I'll check the route-plan client spans next: which ones have a matched server child, and how long each takes.

input.query: WITH c AS (SELECT trace_id, span_id, service_name cs, span_name cn, time ct, duration cd FROM abnormal_traces WHERE attr_span_kind='Client' AND service_name IN ('ts-route-plan-service','ts-travel-plan-service','ts-basic-service','ts-food-service','ts-preserve-service')) SELECT c.cs, c.cn, (SELECT count(*) FROM abnormal_traces s WHERE s.trace_id=c.trace_id AND s.parent_span_id=c.span_id AND s.attr_span_kind='Server') has_child, count(*) n, approx_quantile(cd/1e6,0.5) p50, approx_quantile(cd/1e6,0.95) p95 FROM c GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY 1,2,3

content.text: Route-plan's GET is itself waiting on travel-service's GET, so the 2.3 s delay is passed up the chain. Basic-service still has slow server spans that I haven't traced, so I'll identify their callers.

input.query: WITH s AS (SELECT trace_id, span_name, duration, parent_span_id FROM abnormal_traces WHERE service_name='ts-basic-service' AND attr_span_kind='Server') , p AS (SELECT span_id, service_name psvc, span_name pname FROM abnormal_traces) SELECT s.span_name, p.psvc caller, p.pname, count(*) n, approx_quantile(s.duration/1e6,0.5) p50, approx_quantile(s.duration/1e6,0.95) p95 FROM s LEFT JOIN p ON p.span_id=s.parent_span_id GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY n DESC LIMIT 20

content.text: Basic-service is slow for every caller, but its per-call child times look modest. Before deciding the kind, I'll check resource metrics to see whether any pod is saturated. First, the metric names available.

input.query: SELECT 'gauge' t, metric, count(DISTINCT service_name) svcs FROM abnormal_metrics GROUP BY 2 UNION ALL SELECT 'sum', metric, count(DISTINCT service_name) FROM abnormal_metrics_sum GROUP BY 2 UNION ALL SELECT 'hist', metric, count(DISTINCT service_name) FROM abnormal_metrics_histogram GROUP BY 2 ORDER BY 1,2

content.text: Next I'll compare CPU limit utilization per pod, normal vs abnormal, for the services on the slow path.

input.query: SELECT metric, service_name, round(avg(CASE WHEN period='n' THEN value END),3) normal_avg, round(avg(CASE WHEN period='a' THEN value END),3) abn_avg FROM (SELECT 'a' period, * FROM abnormal_metrics UNION ALL SELECT 'n', * FROM normal_metrics) WHERE metric IN ('k8s.pod.cpu_limit_utilization','k8s.pod.memory_limit_utilization') AND service_name IN ('ts-travel-service','ts-route-service','ts-basic-service','ts-route-plan-service','ts-travel-plan-service','ts-food-service','ts-preserve-service','ts-station-service','ts-travel2-service','ts-seat-service') GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY 2,1

content.text: No CPU or memory saturation on the slow path, so these delays are not resource exhaustion. Basic-service's long server spans still lack a clear child, so I'll pull one trace of a slow `/basic/travel` call with full timing.

content.text: Route-plan's quickest-route handler makes several sequential calls, each waiting about 2.3 s on travel-service's GET. Basic-service still has a heavy tail, so I'll check which children explain its slowest server spans.

input.query: WITH bs AS (SELECT trace_id, span_id, duration FROM abnormal_traces WHERE service_name='ts-basic-service' AND attr_span_kind='Server' AND duration>500000000), ch AS (SELECT b.span_id bsid, a.service_name, a.span_name, a.attr_span_kind, a.duration, a.time FROM bs b JOIN abnormal_traces a ON a.trace_id=b.trace_id AND a.parent_span_id IN (SELECT span_id FROM abnormal_traces x WHERE x.trace_id=b.trace_id AND x.service_name='ts-basic-service')) SELECT 'n_slow_basic' k, count(*) n FROM bs UNION ALL SELECT service_name||' '||attr_span_kind||' '||span_name, count(*) FROM ch GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 15

content.text: The slow basic-service spans call station, route, train and price services. I'll compare each child's client-side and server-side durations inside those slow traces to find which hop holds the time.

input.query: WITH bs AS (SELECT trace_id, span_id FROM abnormal_traces WHERE service_name='ts-basic-service' AND attr_span_kind='Server' AND duration>500000000) SELECT c.service_name csvc, c.span_name cname, c.attr_span_kind ck, round(c.duration/1e6,1) cms, s.service_name ssvc, round(s.duration/1e6,1) sms, round(extract(epoch FROM (s.time-c.time))*1000,1) gap_ms FROM abnormal_traces c LEFT JOIN abnormal_traces s ON s.parent_span_id=c.span_id AND s.attr_span_kind='Server' WHERE c.trace_id IN (SELECT trace_id FROM bs) AND c.service_name='ts-basic-service' AND c.attr_span_kind='Client' ORDER BY cms DESC LIMIT 25

**Verdict: the evidence does not support `http_slow` as the distinct kind. It points to `network_delay` on the ts-travel-service → ts-route-service path, with moderate confidence.** The one thing span data cannot exclude is a client-side hold inside travel's HTTP client, which is the part of `http_slow` that would look the same.

**What I checked**

- **Shape of the delay.** The travel→route GET gap (Server start minus Client start, 54 pairs) is about 2,322 ms at p25, 2,324 ms at p50 and 2,374 ms at p95. The client span is 2,309 / 2,312 / 2,565 ms at p25 / p50 / p95, and the route Server span is 5.2 ms at p50. The whole distribution shifted by about 2.3 s, not just the tail. That matches the `network_delay` shape ("the 25th and 50th percentiles move as much as the 95th"). It does not match the loss/corruption shape, where the median stays near normal and the tail jumps in ~200 ms steps.
- **Scope.** Travel's other outbound calls are not delayed by 2.3 s. Its POSTs to ts-basic-service and ts-seat-service have gaps of roughly 8–9 ms at p50. The DB SELECT is about 1 ms. So the slowdown is confined to one peer pair rather than to the pod's HTTP traffic in general.
- **Where the time sits.** Route's own processing is normal (about 5 ms). Travel's own server-side self time is also normal (p95 about 43 ms). The extra time sits between the two ends of the call.
- **Errors.** None. Error share is 0.00 on both sides, and the call rate drop is in line with the overall volume drop across the system.
- **Network metrics.** `hubble_*` has no per-connection series from ts-travel-service to ts-route-service in the abnormal period. Hubble cannot confirm or refute the wire-level explanation. The only travel-related hubble rows are flow counters and a drop-total series for the travel pod, with no drop shift attributed to this pair.

**Why `http_slow` is not supported**

`http_slow` requires that only particular HTTP routes be affected, with the same pod's other traffic to the same peer normal. Here, the only traffic travel sends to route-service is the GET, so there is no other route on that edge to compare against. The "other traffic to the same peer" test cannot be run. What the data does show is that the fault is confined to one peer, which is the connection-level signature.

**Limits**

- Span timestamps cannot separate time on the wire from a hold inside travel's HTTP client before the request is sent. Both would appear as the Client-to-Server gap. There are no TCP RTT or retransmit metrics in this case to resolve that.
- The network-delay reading therefore rests on the uniform percentile shift and the single-peer scope, not on a direct transport measurement.
